CHRONOLOGY.title: COVESA vSomeIP 3.x release evolution
CHRONOLOGY.selection_rationale: Use the release series as maturity chronology rather than a separate architecture story.
remaining_boundaries: Release notes establish project changes, not independent SOME/IP conformance, production deployment scale, safety qualification or comparative performance.

CHRONOLOGY.title: Eclipse S-CORE project launch
CHRONOLOGY.selection_rationale: Use the launch announcement to establish the start of the open core-stack initiative, not as a separate technical package.
remaining_boundaries: The announcement included forward-looking release targets and safety-process goals; those targets are not treated here as proof of later delivery or certification.

CHRONOLOGY.title: Eclipse Safe Open Vehicle Core (S-CORE)
CHRONOLOGY.selection_rationale: Use the S-CORE release series to show maturation across communication, safety, integration and module-maturity mechanisms.
remaining_boundaries: What exact runtime/platform component baseline was delivered in v0.1.0 beyond the existence of the tag/release?
Which S-CORE components had production-grade or safety-qualified status at each release, as distinct from documentation/process maturity?

Release notes are project-authored evidence of repository changes; they do not by themselves establish production deployment, interoperability, functional-safety certification or automotive-grade maturity.
The v0.1.0 release page provides a release and full-changelog link but no detailed release-note body, so its exact technical baseline is unresolved from this source alone.

FEATURE_CORE.title: Centralization potential of automotive E/E architectures
FEATURE_CORE.selection_rationale: Use as the cross-cutting decision framework for how far centralization should proceed and where local/distributed constraints remain.
FEATURE_CORE.organization: Daimler Truck AG / Technical University of Munich / University of Stuttgart
remaining_boundaries: The authors frame the interview analysis as qualitative rather than statistically significant; findings therefore should not be treated as population-level quantitative validation.
The practitioner interview study is tied to Daimler Truck AG and the paper discusses external-generalizability limits; architecture conclusions should be treated as contextual rather than universal.

FEATURE_CORE.title: Deterministic and Reliable Software-Defined Vehicles: key building blocks, challenges, and vision
FEATURE_CORE.selection_rationale: Use as a synthesis anchor for deterministic/reliable SDV building blocks and the coupling between compute, communication and dependability.
FEATURE_CORE.organization: University of Aveiro / Instituto de Telecomunicações
remaining_boundaries: The five-component architecture is a survey-derived vision; the paper discusses validation paths rather than establishing production deployment or end-to-end certification of the complete architecture.
Many architecture-transition statements synthesize cited literature and industry material and should not be treated as independently measured facts from this paper.

SECTION_CORE.title: An OpenSource CI/CD Pipeline for Variant-Rich Software-Defined Vehicles
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Core evidence for variant-aware CI/CD and the development-lifecycle implications of SDV architecture.
remaining_boundaries: The evaluation is a laboratory setup using TurtleBots, ESP32-based ECU emulation and a central backend, not a production vehicle/fleet validation.
The authors explicitly identify deployment to a larger connected-vehicle testbed and deeper feature-model/variant-management integration as future work.

SECTION_CORE.title: CAN XL
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Core non-Ethernet backbone/sub-backbone counterpoint that prevents the network chapter from collapsing into an Ethernet-only story.
remaining_boundaries: The ISO 11898-1:2024 normative text was not available through the pinned Source Intake; this card verifies only the public CiA description and standardization status.

SECTION_CORE.title: COVESA Vehicle Signal Specification v4.1–v6.0 evolution
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Core evidence for stable vehicle-data semantics as software/service boundaries move independently of physical ECU topology.
remaining_boundaries: VSS specifies a vehicle-data taxonomy/model and associated tooling; these releases do not by themselves establish a transport protocol, service runtime, or OEM-wide adoption.

SECTION_CORE.title: Eclipse S-CORE
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Core implementation-platform evidence for the open software foundation emerging around high-performance SDV ECUs.
remaining_boundaries: Statements such as 'production-ready' or predictable/safe behavior are project claims unless backed by separate certification, conformance or deployment evidence.

SECTION_CORE.title: IEEE Std 802.1DG-2025 — Time-Sensitive Networking Profile for Automotive In-Vehicle Ethernet Communications
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Published automotive-specific TSN profile is a primary standard anchor for deterministic Ethernet.
remaining_boundaries: Which detailed mandatory/optional TSN feature selections and configuration parameters are normative in the full IEEE Std 802.1DG-2025 text?
This verification used public IEEE project/publication pages; detailed normative requirements and parameter values in the full standard were not independently inspected.

SECTION_CORE.title: Towards Mixed-Criticality Software Architectures for Centralized HPC Platforms in Software-Defined Vehicles: A Systematic Literature Review
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Core evidence for mixed-criticality integration on centralized HPC and for the safety/isolation constraints on consolidation.
remaining_boundaries: The review does not apply snowballing and excludes some inaccessible/non-English material, including Chinese-language papers and SAE reports; the authors acknowledge publication-bias risk.

The authors note that limited public industry data hinders validation of recent automotive software-architecture advances and that gray literature/expert interviews could improve current-practice coverage.
Best practices transferred from avionics/cloud and the review's applicability outside automotive require further investigation.

SECTION_CORE.title: Virtualization & Microservice Architecture for Software-Defined Vehicles: An Evaluation and Exploration
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Core empirical evidence for virtualization and microservice trade-offs on SDV compute platforms.
SECTION_CORE.organization: Technical University of Munich / collaborating institutions
remaining_boundaries: The paper shows different start-up behavior on AMD64 and ARM64, so the percentages are not portable across hardware/runtime configurations without retesting.
The authors explicitly find that the best microservice/container count is neither necessarily the maximum nor minimum and must be determined experimentally.
The study is a performance evaluation, not evidence that virtualization/containerization automatically satisfies automotive safety isolation, certification, or deterministic timing requirements.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: An Investigation of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform from an Industry Perspective
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Industry-perspective evidence is useful for AUTOSAR Adaptive friction and adoption context, but remains partial and should not anchor normative claims.
remaining_boundaries: Inspect the full paper for minimal-AP components, industry context, detailed pain-point taxonomy, attribution evidence and threats to validity.

The accessible primary abstract does not expose the minimal-AP implementation scope, participant/industry context, concrete pain-point inventory, trace from each pain point to specification/vendor/local causes, or study validity discussion.
Findings explicitly mix specification, vendor implementation and local practice; they should not be generalized as intrinsic AUTOSAR Adaptive defects without item-level attribution.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: ASIL-Decomposition Based Resource Allocation Optimization for Automotive E/E Architectures
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports the mixed-criticality section with an ASIL-decomposition/resource-allocation optimization example.
remaining_boundaries: For simplicity, the model assumes coexistence/freedom-from-interference criteria are satisfied when mixed-criticality tasks share hardware; the optimization does not itself establish the complete safety argument for that coexistence.
Scalability experiments use a fixed four-ECU architecture with randomly generated task graphs and randomized WCET/WCRT/cost values, limiting direct transfer to a production E/E program.
Reported objective values and solver timings are case-study/problem-instance results rather than universal design-space optimization performance.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: AUTOFRAME — A Software-driven Integration Framework for Automotive Systems
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports software-driven integration and configuration as a bridge between platform architecture and development tooling.
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.organization: Technical University of Munich / IIT Mandi
remaining_boundaries: The evaluation uses CARLA and workstation-class hardware to emulate the vehicle/sensor-actuator environment; it does not establish behavior on production automotive compute or physical vehicle buses.

The authors list stronger cybersecurity measures, throughput/processing optimization and reliable real-time operation as future work, so those properties are not fully established by the current evaluation.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: Automatic Platform Configuration and Software Integration for Software-Defined Vehicles
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports automated platform configuration/integration and its resource/safety constraints.
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.organization: Technical University of Munich / University of Bamberg
remaining_boundaries: The demonstration is a simulated SDV environment; the authors explicitly identify a more comprehensive demonstration with realistic automotive hardware and software as future work.

The authors note that online integration on the vehicle may be restricted to relatively small problems because vehicle compute resources are limited; larger-scale analysis is better suited to design time.
The PoC predefines VMs because the selected ACRN setup has limited runtime configuration flexibility.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: Automotive Middleware Performance: Comparison of FastDDS, Zenoh and vSomeIP
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Provides comparative middleware performance evidence for the consequences of choosing different communication substrates.
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.organization: RWTH Aachen University / associated AUTOtechagil project
remaining_boundaries: Results are configuration- and Linux-testbed-specific; the authors identify embedded-platform evaluation as future work.

Two configurations were omitted as not meaningful: vSomeIP best-effort above the small-message case because SOME/IP-TP was not implemented, and Zenoh reliable because the selected reliable configuration did not affect transmission.
The paper itself shows topology/data-rate dependent reversals, so its measurements should not be generalized into a single universal middleware ranking.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: AUTOSAR AP and ROS 2 Collaboration Framework
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports interoperability discussion at the AUTOSAR Adaptive/ROS 2 boundary.
remaining_boundaries: AUTOSAR Adaptive/QNX is evaluated in QEMU rather than on an automotive target ECU/HPC.
The implementation/evaluation is tied to ROS 2 Humble, Fast DDS, vsomeip 3.4.9.1 and AUTOSAR Adaptive R20-11; interoperability across other implementations/releases requires separate evidence.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: Building Automotive Security on Internet Standards: An Integration of DNSSEC, DANE, and DANCE to Authenticate and Authorize In-Car Services
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports service authentication/authorization and trust-boundary discussion using Internet-standard security mechanisms.
remaining_boundaries: The evaluation shows high performance jitter, attributed partly to parallel execution on a single system; Open vSwitch/Mininet emulation also omits physical network transmission times.
Supply-chain attacks, secure builds, OTA distribution and some mixed-security downgrade cases are outside the detailed security analysis.
The main automotive evaluation does not include remote DNSSEC resolution in the service-setup path; the authors expect such resolution to occur during update procedures.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: CARISMA: CAR-Integrated Service Mesh Architecture
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports cloud-native/service-mesh influence on in-vehicle service architecture without making it the survey thesis.
remaining_boundaries: What latency, jitter, CPU/memory overhead and failure-mode behavior would CARISMA exhibit on automotive HPC hardware and deterministic in-vehicle networks?
Validation is a two-VM proof of concept rather than embedded automotive HPC hardware or an in-vehicle network.
The authors explicitly defer a sound evaluation of CARISMA overhead versus direct inter-service communication to future work.
The prototype intentionally uses exactly one proxy per HPC and does not claim redundant proxy behavior.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: COVESA vSomeIP
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Primary project evidence for the SOME/IP implementation layer used in service-oriented in-vehicle communication.
remaining_boundaries: The same page makes broad adoption/deployment statements; this card does not treat those as independently verified production-deployment evidence.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: DENSO deterministic middleware SOAFEE Blueprint
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports cloud-native-to-deterministic-runtime discussion with a concrete SOAFEE/DENSO implementation claim.
remaining_boundaries: The page is authored by DENSO and hosted by SOAFEE; deterministic guarantees and portability/safety benefits are vendor/project claims rather than independent certification evidence.
The pinned article does not provide a sufficiently detailed independent latency/jitter or safety-certification evaluation for quantitative comparison.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: From Code to Road: A Vehicle-in-the-Loop and Digital Twin-Based Framework for Central Car Server Testing in Autonomous Driving
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports the validation-lifecycle section with a central-car-server Vehicle-in-the-Loop/digital-twin example; preserve its partial evidence caveat.
remaining_boundaries: Inspect the full paper for dynamometer/vehicle/server setup, synchronization architecture, case-study metrics, and comparison with conventional ViL/HIL.

The accessible primary text does not expose case-study scenario definitions, central-server hardware, timing/accuracy metrics, synchronization error, comparison baseline, or quantitative development-effort reduction.
The evaluation is centered on autonomous-driving software; conclusions about other centralized vehicle domains require separate evidence.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: Negotiating strict latency limits for dynamic real-time services in vehicular time-sensitive networks
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Provides research evidence for dynamic QoS negotiation under strict latency constraints on vehicular TSN.
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.organization: TU Dresden / HAW Hamburg / TU Eindhoven
remaining_boundaries: The central controller is a potential single point of failure during reservation/setup, although established real-time data paths do not continuously depend on it.
Hard deadline guarantees can require substantial bandwidth overprovisioning relative to less conservative schemes.
Reliable delivery/retransmission is treated as orthogonal to the strict real-time reservation problem, and redundancy mechanisms such as FRER are left for extensions.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: OPEN Alliance TC14 10BASE-T1S automotive specification suite
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports the physical/zonal edge of the Ethernet story with multidrop 10BASE-T1S automotive specifications.
remaining_boundaries: The committee page establishes document scope/version status but does not by itself prove that a specific PHY/ECU product passes the conformance or interoperability suites.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: OPEN Alliance TC9 Automotive Ethernet Channel & Components specifications
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports the network chapter with channel/component constraints that keep logical architecture tied to physical automotive Ethernet reality.
remaining_boundaries: This page verifies channel/component specification activity and versions, not electrical performance of any particular production harness or connector implementation.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: RISC-V Needs Secure 'Wheels': the MCU Initiator-Side Perspective
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports hardware-enforced isolation and trust-boundary discussion for consolidated automotive compute.
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.organization: OSYX Technologies / Universidade do Minho / Infineon AG
remaining_boundaries: The paper explicitly focuses on initiator-side mechanisms and defers resource-side developments.
The open-source QEMU/CPU/Bao proof-of-concept is presented as a roadmap rather than completed validation in this paper.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: SDVDiag: A Modular Platform for the Diagnosis of Connected Vehicle Functions
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Supports diagnostics as a modular software-defined vehicle service and lifecycle concern.
remaining_boundaries: The evaluation is a controlled 5G test-fleet/smart-charging scenario with injected faults rather than broad production-fleet fault distributions.
Graph-based rankings identify likely root causes; their correctness depends on dependency/causal graph quality, anomaly detection, and the selected analysis module.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Modular Drive Architecture for Software-defined Vehicles Enabled by Power-packet-based Sensorless Control
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence is credible but the power-packet/sensorless-drive architecture is peripheral to the survey's E/E responsibility-boundary thesis and would dilute the 48-page volume.
remaining_boundaries: Robust information-tag transmission under electromagnetic noise is identified as a practical requirement; error-correction redundancy was omitted from the experimental implementation.
The method assumes one excitation phase is magnetized at a time; simultaneous multi-phase excitation is future protocol work.
The experiment is a laboratory SRM/power-router bench, not an automotive drive-unit durability, EMC, fault-safety or production-vehicle validation.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: A Centralized Discovery-Based Method for Integrating Data Distribution Service and Time-Sensitive Networking in In-Vehicle Networks
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: Verify the full experimental topology/hardware, TSN configuration, traffic load, latency/jitter distributions and exact automated-configuration timing from the full paper.
This pass verified only the author abstract/metadata; exact topology, hardware, traffic load, latency/jitter values and threats to validity remain unresolved.
The phrase 'traditional Ethernet' in the abstract is insufficient to reconstruct the exact baseline configuration without the full evaluation section.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: A Containerized Microservice Architecture for a ROS 2 Autonomous Driving Software: An End-to-End Latency Evaluation
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
not_selected_for_architecture.organization: Technical University of Munich / collaborating institutions
remaining_boundaries: Inspect the full paper to verify hardware, ROS 2 topology, container/runtime configuration, jitter and resource-utilization measurements, statistical treatment, and explicit limitations.
This pass verified the primary abstract but did not reconstruct the full hardware/software setup, workload, jitter distributions, CPU/memory results, or statistical treatment.
The reported latency result is tied to the paper's presented autonomous-driving application and must not be generalized to containerization in all automotive workloads.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Chiplets on Wheels: Review Paper on Holistic Chiplet Solutions for Autonomous Vehicles
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: This verification established the contribution set from the primary abstract but did not reconstruct workload definitions, chiplet interconnect assumptions, thermal models, latency/throughput results, or comparative baselines.
The work primarily concerns silicon/chiplet architecture rather than the vehicle-level allocation of I/O, network, software services, and lifecycle responsibilities.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Computation-Accuracy Trade-Off in Service-Oriented Model-Based Control
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: Inspect the full paper for service graph, control-error/computation metrics, deadline model, optimization overhead and execution platform.

The accessible primary abstract does not expose the control-plant model, service alternatives, hardware/runtime platform, objective values, search/runtime overhead, accuracy metrics, or real-time deadline results.
The demonstrated application is a longitudinal-velocity control case and should not be generalized to all mixed-criticality vehicle functions.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Contextualizing Security and Privacy of Software-Defined Vehicles: A Literature Review and Industry Perspectives
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
not_selected_for_architecture.organization: CNR / Clemson University / TUM / collaborating institutions
remaining_boundaries: The 11-response purposive expert sample is explicitly indicative rather than statistically generalizable.
Architecture/security statements summarize literature and practitioner judgment and should not substitute for normative standards or direct implementation evidence.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: COVESA 2024 ecosystem highlights
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: This is a consortium year-in-review and mixes technical, membership, event and marketing milestones; it is stronger for ecosystem chronology than for architecture mechanics.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Deterministic Task Scheduling in In-Vehicle Networks for Software-Defined Vehicles
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: Inspect the full paper for task/network model, hard-deadline metric, topology sizes, numerical comparison results, wireless assumptions, and solver/runtime complexity.

The accessible primary abstract does not expose scheduling formulation, topology sizes, task/deadline distributions, deterministic-service metric, wireless parameters, numerical gains, or computational complexity.
The abstract's hybrid wireless-wired result should not be generalized to production IVN reliability/safety without detailed channel and interference assumptions.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Efficient Integration of cross platform functions onto service-oriented architectures
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: Inspect the full paper's integration-efficiency metrics, baseline/manual workflow, toolchain and example-application setup before quantitative use.
The accessible primary abstract states that efficiency metrics are presented but does not expose their definitions, baseline, numerical values, toolchain effort, or experimental conditions.

A single example integration does not establish general integration cost or portability across arbitrary AUTOSAR vendor stacks, Classic/Adaptive releases, ROS 2 distributions, or production E/E programs.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Enhancing Automotive User Experience with Dynamic Service Orchestration for Software Defined Vehicles
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: The primary abstract does not expose enough detail to reconstruct scenario size, baselines, compute hardware, objective normalization, or runtime distributions.
A subsequent 2024 paper by the same authors presents dedicated test-bench validation, making this initial simulation study less suitable as the main empirical evidence for industrial feasibility.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Experimental Validation of User Experience-focused Dynamic Onboard Service Orchestration for Software Defined Vehicles
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: The primary abstract states that a dedicated test bench was used but does not expose its hardware/network composition, workload, baselines, measured execution times, or QoS outcomes.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: SISSA: Real-time Monitoring of Hardware Functional Safety and Cybersecurity with In-vehicle SOME/IP Ethernet Traffic
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: The evaluation uses generated SOME/IP traffic with simulated attacks and random-hardware-failure windows; it does not establish behavior on diverse production-vehicle traffic or real hardware failures.
The paper focuses on SOME/IP and proposes CAN/general-protocol expansion as future work.
The paper notes that the best LSTM+attention model may occasionally misclassify normal operation as faulty and attributes this to possible overfitting.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: The Rise of the Software-Defined Vehicle: Architectures, Enabling Technologies, and Future Opportunities
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: Inspect the full survey methodology/source corpus before using it as systematic evidence rather than contextual synthesis.
This is a broad survey rather than primary empirical validation of any one architecture mechanism.
The accessible primary abstract does not expose search methodology, source-selection criteria, study count, evidence-quality assessment, or threats to validity.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Towards Intelligent Computation Offloading in Dynamic Vehicular Networks: A Scalable Multilayer Pipeline
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: Inspect full paper for RTT constraints, function classes, network/mobility model, response-time and success-rate results, baseline complexity, and safety boundary.

The accessible primary abstract does not expose round-trip-time thresholds, mobility traces, task workloads, brute-force search budget, response-time values, success-rate values, or offloading-network assumptions.
The work motivates safety-critical workloads but the abstract does not establish a safety case for offloading safety-critical control functions.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Towards Timing Isolation for Mixed-Criticality Communication in Software-Defined Vehicles
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: The primary abstract does not expose hardware, Linux/kernel/NIC versions, traffic load, latency/jitter distributions, CPU cost, or comparison baselines needed for complete performance verification.
The demonstrated architecture is DDS/Linux/XDP/NIC-queue specific; portability to other middleware, kernels and NICs requires separate evidence.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: zk-ScalHard: Scalable and Hardware-Rooted Privacy-Preserving Authentication for Secure OTA Updates in Zonal SDVs
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: Inspect the full v2 report/repository for threat model, ZKP circuits, proof/prover/verifier costs, topology scale, Uptane baseline and definitions behind the 99.2%/99.9% results.

The accessible primary abstract does not expose cryptographic security assumptions, benchmark ECU/zonal topology, proof sizes, prover/verifier hardware, latency/energy costs, Uptane configuration, or exact definition of temporal attack surface.
Claims of 100% data sovereignty, GDPR compliance and the very large percentage reductions are author claims and require full methodology/security-model inspection before editorial use.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Zonal Architecture Development with evolution of Artificial Intelligence
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence remains HOLD/INSPECT_MORE; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: The paper is primarily a narrative overview drawing on prior literature and does not present a controlled E/E architecture experiment that independently validates its broad performance, reliability, or cost claims.
A substantial part of the paper focuses on neural networks, autonomous driving, edge computing and sensor fusion; only the E/E responsibility-boundary portions are relevant to this survey.
Some broad assertions in the paper are stronger than the evidence shown; they should remain AUTHOR_CLAIM and not be repeated as established facts without stronger primary support.

rules: Issue Architecture may group several selected items into one comparison package.
Supporting evidence is not a duplicate story and need not receive its own article package.
Do not add HOLD_OUT or EXCLUDE items without a new Selection revision bound to an updated matrix.
No section quota is required; weak sections may be omitted.
Article drafting begins only after the Architecture Plan validates successfully.
